channel.title: The Lowndes Signal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Lowndes Signal (lowndessignal.com)

item.title: Black History program wows Fort Deposit community
item.description: Fort Deposit Elementary’s immersive “Journey Through Black History” program, with live actors and interactive hallways, wowed the community and went viral on social media.

item.title: March marks Developmental Disabilities Awareness month
item.description: March is Developmental Disabilities Awareness Month in Alabama, highlighting 120,000 residents and ADMH services that support independence, community life and lifelong opportunities.

item.title: Drug Court celebrates 25 years of second chances
item.description: Second Judicial District Drug Court marks 25 years and 300+ graduates, using treatment, accountability and community support to offer an alternative to prison for people battling addiction.

item.title: The command was issued
item.description: Rev. R.A. Mathews reflects on Iraq airstrikes, Daniel’s vision, and what the Bible says about heaven, angels, and a God who hears our prayers.

item.title: Turn around, look at me
item.description: A frog fable, a jealous church member, and biblical lessons on ego show why seeking credit can cost more than it gives, and why believers are called to serve for God, not applause.

item.title: Lowndes County students celebrate Black history
item.description: Lowndes County schools marked Black History Month with themed dress days, performances, guest speakers and student tributes to civil rights leaders across multiple campuses.

item.title: Voting open for athlete contest
item.description: Vote now for Lowndes County Athlete of the Week: support Ayala Johnson, Grant Casey or Cedricus Jenkins once every hour online through Tuesday at noon.

item.title: Return to the 'old paths'
item.description: Jeremiah’s call to the “old paths” is applied today as a plea for Christians to leave denominational divisions and return to simple New Testament Christianity.

item.title: Ordinary in our hands, extraordinary in God’s
item.description: A pastor reflects on how God uses ordinary lives — like fishermen, teachers, parents, and mechanics — to do extraordinary work when we place our lives in His hands.

item.title: Pate awarded nutrition school friend of the year
item.description: Alabama Agriculture Commissioner Rick Pate named ASNA Friend of the Year for leading the Farm to School Incentive Program, boosting fresh Alabama-grown foods in cafeterias statewide.
